Container.Name: overseer
Container.Overview: Overseer serves documents that are data, layout and logic at once - trackers, lists, project boards - with the page to read and change them and a JSON API for programs. Set OVERSEER_TOKEN, the server's master key, and OVERSEER_ADMIN, the username you will sign in with: the log then holds a link to make that account. Programs get keys of an account, made in the page's account drawer. See DEPLOYING.md in the repository.

Config.Name: Web page
Config.Description: The port of the page and the API.

Config.Name: Documents
Config.Description: The documents, a folder per person, and the server's own settings. A share instead of appdata reaches them over SMB too.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: The accounts file, with the password hashes: kept out of the documents and their backups.

Config.Name: Cache
Config.Description: Worked-out documents, kept across restarts. Many small files: on a cache pool.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: The user id the server runs as and its files belong to; 99 is Unraid's nobody. Never 0.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: The group id; 100 is Unraid's users.

Config.Name: OVERSEER_TOKEN
Config.Description: The server's master key: whoever holds it may do anything. A long random string (openssl rand -hex 32). Give programs an account's key instead.

Config.Name: OVERSEER_ADMIN
Config.Description: The username of the account that may invite others. Until it exists, the log holds a link to make it.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: The time zone documents read their dates in.

Config.Name: OVERSEER_ACCOUNTS
Config.Description: Where the accounts file is, in the container.

Config.Name: OVERSEER_DISK_CACHE
Config.Description: Where worked-out documents are kept, in the container; empty keeps none.
